params.body:
The brief was built from the screen's cards alone: an agent read titles made for eyes ("Weakest pages") and Portal kept a table (`MEETSLEUTEL`) to turn them back into measurement keys. Shane asked why the agent side maps to the human screens at all.

Version 2 adds, without renaming anything of version 1:

- `catalogue`: what Elixir measures, as Elixir declares it, by key (concern, cost, decay, cadence, triggers, dependsOn, needs).
- per watched project `measurements`: every measurement Elixir wrote, under its key, with state, moments, facts verbatim (lists over 30 cut with a marker) and the dashboard's `verdict` on those facts: the worst of the cards that read the key, so brief and screen cannot disagree. `staging` alongside when it ran there. Null for an unwatched project, not an empty map.
- every task carries `measurementKey`, the key `measure --only` takes.

The cards stay as the rendering for a screen; the markdown brief is unchanged. Contract in `docs/fleet-brief.md`, test in `FleetBriefTest`. Suite green (BuildStampTest fails only in this worktree), PHPStan green.

Proposed through the control gateway under #agent-workbench.
params.title: De fleet brief spreekt in metingen (versie 2)
